identifying_markers: Distinct spectacle mark on dorsal hood
first_aid: Immobilize the bitten limb immediately with a splint below heart level.
Apply broad pressure-immobilization bandage over the bite area (do not occlude arterial pulse).
Do NOT cut, suck venom, or apply tight tourniquets.
Keep victim calm and still to slow lymphatic venom spread.
Transport immediately to nearest hospital with Polyvalent Anti-Venom Serum (AVS).
notes: Responsible for the largest number of neurotoxic snake envenomations in India. Part of the 'Big Four'.

identifying_markers: Flat triangular head distinct from neck
Deep brown chain-like circular spots in 3 longitudinal rows
symptoms: Severe immediate burning pain & massive localized swelling
Spontaneous systemic bleeding from gums & bite wound
first_aid: Keep affected limb completely still and splinted.
Do NOT apply arterial tourniquet (causes localized gangrene and tissue loss).
Remove rings, tight jewelry, or tight clothing immediately before swelling increases.
Administer 20-minute whole blood clotting test (20WBCT) on hospital arrival.
Immediate transport to emergency trauma center with AVS and dialysis readiness.
notes: Causes profound coagulopathy and acute renal failure. Part of the 'Big Four'.

region: Rural habitations, agricultural fields, floor sleeping mats (nocturnal)
identifying_markers: Glossy steel-black or dark bluish-brown body
Distinct narrow paired white cross-bands along spine
Enlarged hexagonal vertebral scales down middle of back
symptoms: Painless nocturnal bite (often mistaken for insect bite)
first_aid: Immediate emergency medical evacuation even if bite puncture is painless or invisible.
Prepare for emergency assisted mechanical ventilation / intubation.
Do NOT delay hospital transit for non-symptom observation.
Polyvalent AVS administration is urgently required.
notes: 15x more lethal than Cobra venom. Envenomation occurs almost exclusively at night while victims sleep on the floor. Part of the 'Big Four'.

region: Dry semi-arid regions, rocks, red soil, scrub forests
identifying_markers: White cruciform or bird-foot mark on crown of head
Serrated flank scales that produce raspy sawing noise
first_aid: Immobilize limb with broad splint.
Avoid NSAIDs / Aspirin (drastically worsens systemic hemorrhage).
Expedited evacuation to hospital with Polyvalent AVS.
notes: Smallest of the Big Four venomous snakes, but causes high morbidity in arid zones. Part of the 'Big Four'.

region: Dense forests, Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, Terai regions
identifying_markers: Chevron band pattern on dark olive-brown body
symptoms: Rapid onset flaccid paralysis within 15-30 mins
first_aid: Immediate emergency airway management & mechanical ventilation.
Immobilize patient completely; do not allow walking.
Requires high-dose Antivenom titration.
notes: World's longest venomous snake. Venom yield can kill an adult Asian elephant within hours.

region: Bamboo groves, coffee/tea plantations, Western Ghats
identifying_markers: Heat-sensing loreal pit between eye and nostril
symptoms: Intense local burning pain and localized edema
Bruising and blistering around bite mark
first_aid: Wash surface gently; splint limb.
Do NOT apply ice packs or incisions.
Observe in hospital for systemic coagulopathy progression.
notes: Arboreal viper responsible for plantation worker envenomations in southern and western India.

region: Agricultural fields, gardens, urban peripheries, godowns
identifying_markers: Large yellowish-brown body with black net-like tail markings
Large round eyes with golden iris
symptoms: NO neurotoxic or hemotoxic systemic symptoms
first_aid: Wash wound thoroughly with clean tap water and antiseptic soap.
Apply mild antiseptic solution and clean sterile dry dressing.
Verify Tetanus Toxoid (TT) vaccination status.
Reassure victim that the species is non-venomous.
notes: Frequently mistaken for Spectacled Cobra due to size and speed, but completely harmless and vital agricultural rodent controller.

region: Scrublands, urban hedges, agricultural tree edges
identifying_markers: Chocolate brown body with dark reticulated cross-bands and white speckling
Dual black streaks radiating from eye
first_aid: Cleanse bite scratches with antiseptic.
Dress with sterile gauze.
Administer Tetanus shot if booster expired.
notes: Non-venomous colubrid snake often displaying an 'S'-shaped defensive coil.
